name: LLVM
summary: A compiler infrastructure centered on a typed SSA-based intermediate representation and composable analysis and transformation passes between language front ends and target code generation.

features.name: Typed SSA intermediate representation
features.description: LLVM IR is a typed, low-level, SSA-based representation used as a common code representation across compilation phases. The representation has in-memory, bitcode, and human-readable assembly forms.
benefits: Gives analyses and transformations a shared, language-independent representation
Supports verification and serialization across compiler tools
costs: Front ends must lower higher-level language semantics into a lower-level representation
IR well-formedness and target-specific semantics constrain transformations

features.name: Analysis and transformation pass pipeline
features.description: LLVM organizes compiler work into analysis, transform, and utility passes. Analysis passes compute information, while transform passes may mutate the program and interact with analysis results.
benefits: Allows reusable analyses to support multiple transformations
Makes optimization behavior inspectable as a sequence of bounded transformations
costs: Transformations can invalidate analyses and require dependency management
Pass ordering and target assumptions affect optimization outcomes

features.name: Front-end and back-end boundary
features.description: LLVM's documented system accepts IR from language front ends and provides tools, libraries, and headers to process IR and convert it into object files, with target-specific code generation at the back end.
benefits: Permits multiple front ends to share middle-end infrastructure
Separates language lowering concerns from target code generation
costs: The shared boundary must preserve enough semantics for different languages and targets
Interfaces expose compatibility and target-feature coordination costs

mathematical_views.question: How can compiler analyses and transformations operate on a shared representation of typed values and control flow?
assumptions: An LLVM module can be abstracted as typed values, basic blocks, control-flow edges, and uses
The model treats verifier conditions and undefined-behavior details as explicit preconditions
The graph abstraction omits layout and target-specific lowering details

mathematical_views.question: When does a sequence of LLVM passes preserve the intended program behavior while changing its representation or cost?
assumptions: Each transformation has a documented or implementation-defined validity precondition
Analysis results are treated as conditional knowledge that may be invalidated by mutation
The view describes a candidate refinement relation and does not establish equivalence for arbitrary passes

benefits: Shared representation for optimization, verification, and serialization
costs: Lowering and well-formedness rules add compiler complexity
Pass invalidation and ordering make global behavior harder to reason about

benefits: Reuse across source languages and target architectures
costs: The shared contract must accommodate language and target variation
